<subject>Catherine Storey for Corporate Advisory Cutoff Procedures</subject>
<body>
I spoke with each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this matter was delayed due to other urgent priorities. Nevertheless, everyone agreed that establishing a standard daily cutoff for Corporate Advisory transactions would be beneficial.

The preferred approach is to set the cutoff at 4pm each business day (to provide context, I reviewed yesterday’s activity to see how many transactions were initiated after 4pm London time. We had three UK Corporate mandates and two European cross-border agreements). Transactions logged after 4pm would automatically be recorded as business for the following day. However, for any transactions that do not roll forward automatically after the cutoff, the relevant risk and compliance teams will need to treat these as next-day business. I’m uncertain how this might affect the Compliance unit’s daily position reporting, since official ledgers won’t reflect late-day entries on the same day. Can Compliance generate supplemental reports to ensure advisory teams have accurate client exposure data each morning?

Please share any feedback you have, and in any event, confirm whether the 4pm cutoff works for your respective departments.

Danielle  
x36557

Eric – any concerns about the risk reporting system?  
Mary – we touched on this briefly recently… thoughts?  
</body>
